# REALTIQ — Requirements, Implementation and Commercial Scope Audit

Audit dates: 9–10 October 2026. Launch target: 31 October 2026. Confidential — prepared for Samuel and Savant.

This is a source-based audit and implementation register, not production certification or a supplementary quotation. Only this Markdown deliverable is changed.

## 1. Executive Summary

**31 October cannot responsibly be committed for the complete new specification on the evidence available.** There are 21 calendar days from 10 October; major transaction, profile, Compare, social, fee and ecosystem work remains, with unresolved provider/legal decisions. No mandatory live feature has been quietly deferred.

Existing implementation is substantial: public property/project listings, Mapbox search, buyer/landlord/admin/proxy workspaces, authentication, messaging, title uploads and hashing/registry interfaces, paid title access, instalments, escrow/disputes/refunds, proxy inspections, service cart, notifications, ROI/valuation and analytics. These are real API-connected features, not all mocks. Their current business model differs materially from the new RQS.

Key established mismatches: six property types instead of41; squareFeet instead of enforced sqm; GBP/Any Currency and Featured search filters; loaded-page keyword search; escrow treated as a payment type; mandatory instalment over hardcoded ₦50m; payment without visible bilateral terms lock; all-at-once escrow release; single account role rather than profiles; only Matterport/Realsee provider types; professional profile denying live tours and displaying zero ratings; backend Paystack property/basket routing and early Sold/Owned transition.

New commercial candidates include Compare, social feeds/posts, expanded Agency/Partner/public profile families, unit-type inheritance/bulk multi-unit purchase/shared escrow, recurring plans/seats, the fee engine/revenue/tax operations, advanced accounting, and specified ecosystem security/contracts. Original escrow, title hashing, proxy inspections, map discovery, vaults, ROI and planned ecosystem integrations must not be re-billed merely because unfinished. Monetisation was explicitly pending in the original baseline.


Reconciled inventory: **1252 primary entries**. Fully verified end-to-end: **0**. Status counts: Unverified: 582; Incorrect: 199; Missing: 411; Partial: 38; Implemented but not verified: 4; Blocked: 18. Scope: S3: 211; S4: 657; S1: 11; S5: 60; S2: 27; S6: 263; S7: 5; S8: 18. These counts are not percentages of code completion. “Unverified” includes existing modules whose precise new behaviour was not proven, not assumed missing backend functionality. Detailed metrics and caveats follow in §20.

## 2. Audit Methodology and Evidence

Read order followed: entire new PRD including appendices; Specifications §0.1–§0.4; RQS-01–08; complete original baseline; cross-reference and code inspection. Physical PDF page numbers are used throughout. Poppler layout extraction was followed by PyMuPDF sorted text, page metadata, rendering and cell-based table extraction. All required pages contain text. No password-protected or blank unreadable page was found. Layout extraction alone scrambled several multi-column tables; it was not treated as reliable row association.


| Exact document | Pages/text inspected | Extraction | Tables | Diagrams/appendices | Limit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| REALTIQ PRD.pdf | 180/180 | Complete text; bounded page reads | Multi-column tables read and relevant rendered pages checked; Appendix A pp176–179 visually inspected | All16 labelled figures inspected; Appendix B p180 included | Not every table cell visually rechecked at full size |
| REALTIQ Specifications.pdf |169/169|Complete text; front matter before parts|230 tables /1883 nonempty rows extracted;118 explicit08-* rows recovered; continuation rows stitched for onboarding|Ecosystem diagram p135 inspected; notice p169 included; all8 parts present|Automatic tables require final field-by-field implementation validation; no unread page is knowingly omitted|
| REALTIQ Features List Version 2.pdf |5/5|Complete text|No substantive tabular requirements|Both map reference screenshots p2 and ecosystem diagram p5 inspected; all pages rendered/reviewed|Conditional viewer and monetisation “pending” wording retained|


Temporary extraction, rendering, library installation and build output were confined to the permitted Windows Temp directory. No dependency or lockfile in either application repository was installed or rewritten. Existing audit documents were not accepted as implementation proof.

Code inspection covered manifest/entry/provider composition, route/role guards, catalogue hook/forms/filter/map code, project payload/page/manage/import code, payment/cart/instalment/escrow clients and workflows, auth storage, title upload/access/registry, virtual-tour provider/types/viewers/settings, proxy/public professional flows, trust/reviews, messaging/moderation, notifications/personalisation, ROI/AVM/analytics and admin operations. Repository-wide searches checked omitted surfaces, provider names, environment variable usages, TODO/FIXME and mock imports. Not every line of every source or test file was independently read; precise unproven acceptance behaviours are marked accordingly.


A sibling backend at `../realtiq-backend` is readable and was inspected selectively, separate from frontend findings. It is outside the frontend root. Inspected manifest/models/payment/cart/escrow/message/provider evidence establishes some gaps. It is **not** an exhaustive backend audit and no backend test/DB/provider operation was run. Other server-side requirements are **Not verified — backend repository/architecture and deployment evidence required**, even though this sibling exists.

## 3. Source-of-Truth and Document Hierarchy

For intended implementation, detailed RQS takes precedence over PRD. All differences remain visible in §11; conflicting RQS rules require Samuel’s decision. PRD §2.4 and Specifications §0.2 govern live versus implemented-disabled scope. Test fee values are not live fee prices.

For commercial inclusion, the primary evidence is **REALTIQ Features List Version 2.pdf**. The PRD/RQS define mandatory technical delivery, not automatic entitlement to unpaid expansion. No signed price, statement of work, payment receipt, staffing agreement or change order was supplied. S1 explicit; S2 reasonable professional necessity; S3 clarification; S4 substantial expansion; S5 new module; S6 new technical/operational obligation; S7 reversal/replacement; S8 contractual uncertainty. Classifications are evidence-based negotiation guidance, not legal determinations.

|RQS-06|1. Integration-ready from day one. The identifiers, events, APIs and controls in this section are live at launch, even before anything connects. Nothing should have to be — p135|542 family entries; source-specific refs in §6|Read/indexed|

|RQS-06|2. REALTIQ works on its own. Every REALTIQ feature works with no connected application. A connection adds to REALTIQ; it never becomes a dependency. — p136|542 family entries; source-specific refs in §6|Read/indexed|

|RQS-06|3. Shared services, separate modules. Identity, verification records, payments, notifications and data are built as separate modules with their own interfaces, so they can — p136|542 family entries; source-specific refs in §6|Read/indexed|

|RQS-06|4. One account, many roles. A single verified account can hold several roles, on REALTIQ and later in connected applications, without registering again. — p136|542 family entries; source-specific refs in §6|Read/indexed|

|RQS-06|5. REALTIQ owns the contracts. Connected applications build to REALTIQ’s published contracts. REALTIQ does not change to suit each connection. — p136|542 family entries; source-specific refs in §6|Read/indexed|

|RQS-06|23.3 What REALTIQ provides at launch — p136|542 family entries; source-specific refs in §6|Read/indexed|

## 6. Detailed Gap Analysis

Each ID below is a primary delivery/audit task. Module-level current evidence is stated explicitly; per-row status never means a backend endpoint was tested merely because an API client exists. References point to physical pages and source functions/components. Implementation acceptance includes happy path, failure, permissions, persistence and specified business outcomes. For ambiguous rules, resolve the linked discrepancy before coding dependent behaviour.

### 03 — Search query, location and ranking rules

Sources: RQS-03 §§1–3,6–7, pp59–70,74–75; PRD §6.1–6.7,6.10 pp27–34,36–38. Original baseline: §4 pp2–3; §5 p3.

Observed: PropertyFiltersPanel offers six types, four legacy completion stages, Any Currency/GBP and Featured controls. Listings filters keyword text against its loaded ten-result page. useProperties calls the catalogue API for other predicates, but has no URL state. Mapbox clustering/click previews are implemented; selected card state is not passed back as a marker-highlight prop.

Evidence: `src/pages/public/Listings.tsx:19`; `src/components/property/PropertyFiltersPanel.tsx:6`; `src/hooks/useProperties.ts:15`; `src/services/propertyService.ts:29`.

Dependency: MongoDB query/facet and geographic contract changes, gazetteer lifecycle, FX feed and rank settings required. S3 ordinary detail is included unless the explicit additional search controls are commercially agreed as material expansion.

### 04 — Listing onboarding shared rules

Sources: RQS-04 Sections A–M, pp76–87; PRD §7.1–7.8 pp39–48. Original baseline: §5 p3; §1 p1.

Observed: PropertyForm validates price>0, at least one bedroom/bathroom, squareFeet>0 and media presence. It defaults apartment/one room/finished, offers GBP and only available/sold editing, accepts free location and amenities, and forces instalment over ₦50m. It also stages private title uploads with file size/type checks and contains off-plan metadata.

Evidence: `src/components/property/PropertyForm.tsx:21`; `src/utils/propertyPaymentTypes.ts:3`; `src/components/property/StructuredFactsFields.tsx:3`.

Dependency: Property schema/API migration, private field projections, validation parity, review queues and payment/transaction state enforcement. Individual table fields appear below as separate entries.

## 10. Separate Billing / Change Request Candidates

No monetary rates are invented. An unimplemented original feature is not a change request merely because it is unfinished. Normal validation, error handling and responsive presentation remain professional delivery obligations. Detailed candidate entries in §6 record exact requirement/new outcome, closest baseline, additional frontend/server work, dependencies, complexity and confidence.


### A. Clearly outside original scope

Compare is absent from the original list: RQS-05 complete set/table/FX/suggestions/sales/sync/insights. Social authoring and Following/Explore are not promised by a blog/retention heading: RQS-01 §27.2; RQS-06 §17.7. Quote them as distinct product packages, with reusable listing/profile components credited. Confidence high for new modules; medium for reused foundations.

### B. Material expansions likely requiring additional billing

RQS-02 unit-type inheritance/generation/virtualised spreadsheet workspace; RQS-01 bundle negotiation/multi-unit checkout/per-unit ledger/shared verification/dispute propagation; RQS-06 agencies/mandates/new regulated Partner services/paid seats/public profile families/advanced finance. Original basic listings, escrow and proxy remain included. Request acceptance boundaries and incremental effort, rather than quoting entire pre-existing modules again.

### C. Replacement/rework caused by changed requirements

Always-Free development masterplans versus originally Paid (§4 p3); sales-only versus tenancy agreements (§5 p3); default-disabled map viewport search versus automatic map-list updates (§4 pp2–3). Confirm consumed effort and mutually agreed replacement credit before billing rework. Squared-feet code migration is required, but original baseline never specifies sqft: it is not evidence of a client reversal by itself.

### D. Technical/infrastructure additions requiring commercial review

RQS-08 detailed monetisation engine, subscription/seat billing, supplier VAT/invoices/WHT/revenue recognition and fee recovery; RQS-06 §23 OIDC/outbox/OpenAPI/mTLS/HMAC/consent/sandbox contracts; explicit SLA/restore/capacity evidence; additional named provider adapters. Existing ecosystem intent and professional security are already baseline considerations; quote only proven additional architecture/operations.

### E. Ambiguous items requiring negotiation

All “pending” monetisation decisions, advanced analytics omitted/refined by the new source, conditional native viewer, offline PWA/heatmaps/Lidar/news, provider commercial costs and new operational departmental staffing. Obtain the original accepted estimate/change history and confirm included effort.

Recommended supplementary quotation packages: CR1 Compare; CR2 social/public profiles/moderation; CR3 developer inventory and bulk transactions; CR4 escrow/mandates/regulated Partner expansion; CR5 fee engine/plans/finance/tax/provider routing; CR6 ecosystem contracts/security/consent; CR7 approved reversals/migration; CR8 operational/integration assurance. Attach relevant AUD IDs and acceptance, dependencies, exclusions, client/provider licences, complexity ranges and re-used baseline credit. Do not price implementation and third-party recurring charges as the same item.

## 11. PRD/RQS Contradictions

The PRD is not independently treated as an alternative specification. Its §25 A1–A10 explicitly acknowledges several RQS inconsistencies; these are not ten proven PRD-versus-RQS behavioural reversals. This register distinguishes contradiction, omission and ambiguity. No separate direct PRD/RQS contradiction was conclusively established beyond the acknowledged/inherited differences below; RQS internal conflicts remain unresolved. Resolved distinctions (Sponsored vs Featured, masterplans always Free despite other Paid media, Zoom allowlisted links vs ordinary off-platform links, organic Explore vs paid recommendation placement) are not falsely counted as contradictions.

## 15. Security, Compliance and Non-Functional Gaps

Security follows the new detailed policies and ordinary original professional obligations. Do not automatically bill ordinary authenticated access checks as new scope. The expanded profile/partner/OIDC/consent/segregation architecture is separately reviewable.

- Authorisation: replace sole client role gating with server-checked profile/seat/resource permissions; test object ownership and department boundaries on every action, export, upload and signed URL. Client route hiding alone is insufficient.
- Token/session handling: localStorage JWT/user is observed; assess XSS exposure, server refresh/revocation, logout invalidation, idle/privileged policy and 2FA requirements against PRD §21/RQS-06 Console. No exploit or secure-cookie architecture is asserted without backend evidence.
- Confidentiality: reserve/actual sale/contact/private evidence never leaks via public DTOs, logs, social metadata, notifications or QR pages. Console exceptional visibility must be permissioned and audited.
- Files/providers: validate MIME/content/size server-side, scan uploads, protect private storage, expire signed links and bound embeds/CSP/allowlists; Zoom is an authorised exception to off-platform links.
- Finance: signed callback validation, provider idempotency, immutable fee snapshot and reconciled ledger; no frontend-only amount/role decisions; segregation for sensitive changes/releases/refunds/payouts.
- Privacy: explicit purpose/recipient consent, withdrawal, retention/anonymisation and subject-request handling; counsellor/DPO approval of production data policy. Do not remove legally required transaction evidence by a generic delete.
- Accessibility/responsiveness: keyboard dialogs/maps/tray/tables, focus management, labels/error summaries, contrast in three themes, mobile navigation, usable media fallback and small-screen wizard/Compare. WCAG2.1AA not established by source classes.
- Performance: measured build main JS≈994KB gzip plus provider chunks. Lazy provider import exists, but page/network budgets, server facets, virtualised large unit sets, pagination and image optimisation require realistic measurements; chunk warnings are not alone proof of a breached document SLA.
- Resilience/observability: timeout/retry/cache, deduplicated events, provider outage and failed-payment recovery, redacted structured logs, correlation/global IDs, alerts/runbooks and restore drills. No production load/backup/SLA evidence supplied.
- Quality gate: address one lint error and one warning, retain meaningful existing tests, then add requirement-driven integration/permission/UAT coverage. 289 passing tests verify current test expectations, including mocks, rather than the new complete specification.

## 16. Launch Readiness

### Launch-blocker register

The P0 primary inventory entries are the quantified task-level blockers; related entries are grouped into critical paths here. Provider/legal absence is a dependency blocker rather than a fabricated backend defect.


There are **517 live P0 entries** under this dependency-based prioritisation. Build-disabled foundations remain mandatory, even where P3 reflects activation risk rather than optionality.

| Blocker group | Why launch cannot proceed | Exit evidence |
|---|---|---|
|Identity/authority model|Current roles cannot safely represent new profiles, agencies, seats and departments|Resource-level integration/permission suite and migrated profiles|
|Terms/transaction/completion|Payment and Sold/Owned behaviour conflicts with new legal/terms rules|Bilateral lock, concurrency and completion journey UAT|
|Payments/fees/escrow|Incorrect provider route; unresolved settlement/custody/tax decisions|Approved capabilities and reconciled real sandbox cases|
|Developer bulk/shared transactions|No complete unit inheritance/bundle/per-unit release journey|Multi-unit import, checkout, failure and dispute acceptance|
|Source contradictions/configuration|Publication, fee, currency and release rules unresolved|Signed D register and Console values|
|Integrations/documents|Required Zoom/CloudPano/issuance/verification licensing not established|Licensed real-provider and issued-document verification|
|Ecosystem foundations/security|Required launch foundations are not proven|Backend contract/outbox/auth/consent/switch tests and docs|
|Operations/UAT|No production recovery, security or full acceptance sign-off|Restoration, rollback, permission, responsive and UAT evidence|


### Built-but-disabled register

PRD §2.4 governs Mortgage profiles/capability, referral earning mechanisms, aggregated/anonymised-data product sales and seller-live-tour charging models. Build the stated UI/config/contracts/catalogue and tests; keep production activation off and charging impossible until separate approval. Launch Zoom tours and all three 3D-provider requirements remain live obligations. Future on-platform Zoom Video SDK/Daily/Agora/LiveKit is provider/adapter planning as specified, not assumed a requirement to launch all four vendors. Do not research alternative vendors.


### Critical path, risk and date recommendation

The critical path is business-rule sign-off → canonical profile/property/unit/terms/payment contracts → server persistence/permissions/provider integration → frontend journeys → cross-system verification → UAT/security/recovery → deployment rehearsal. Search, media, Compare, document templates and social UI can proceed in parallel once shared contracts are stable. Provider approval, legal custody and tax decisions cannot be solved by additional frontend developers.

**31 October2026 is not a supportable full-scope commitment.** Current date10October leaves21 calendar days, not21 developer days. Required modules are major additions, and no measured remaining backend effort, dedicated staffing or provider approval schedule exists. Successful compile/build/tests does not alter the missing product model. No feature is made optional to achieve the date.

Use an initial **12–20-week planning range after decisions, staffing and stable contracts**, approximately January–March2027 if mobilisation starts in mid-October, subject to a one-week joint estimation workshop and integration proof. This is a conditional forecast, not an evidence-proven deadline or sum of all per-row estimates. Assume2 frontend engineers,2 backend engineers, dedicated QA, product/design availability and part-time infrastructure/security/provider expertise; less capacity or sequential external approvals pushes the window out. Backend unknowns could materially exceed it. Prefer a two-week proof-and-estimation milestone before approving a contractual date. Any earlier public release requires an explicit negotiated change in launch scope; it cannot be described as full compliance.

Risk: critical—payment/custody and permission model; high—unresolved source rules, third-party approval, bulk financial integrity, ecosystem contracts and migration; medium-high—large client payload/real-provider performance and test coverage; medium—content/theme/label polish. Overall confidence in detecting specified frontend differences is medium-high; in a dated full-stack estimate, low until backend and provider evidence is obtained.

- [ ] **AUD-RQS03-0071** — Build Stage Lifecycle: allowed values Off-plan; Under construction; Uncompleted building; Semi- finished (Advanced Shell / Lock-up); Newly built; Renovated; Previously owned; Old. Control Multi-Select Checkboxes (OR). Rules Default: Any. Unifies physical maturity into 8 lifecycle states, replacing the legacy dual controls (Completion Stage + Listing Type). Semi-finished: exterior fully sealed and secure (lock-up), first-fix plumbing and electrical conduits complete and internal surfaces plastered, with second-fix fixtures, cabinetry, internal doors and decorative finishes not yet installed; distinct from a raw carcass, which is open to the elements. Uncompleted building or Semi-finished listings that will not be completed before handover carry a “Sold as is” label; this is not a separate filter value. Multi-select (buyer filter). — PRD §6.3–6.5 pp28–32 — RQS-03 §3 pp66 — P1 — S3 — Unverified — Live at launch.

- [ ] **AUD-RQS03-0072** — Ready to Move In: allowed values Boolean Macro Chip. Control Preset Filter Macro. Rules Instant macro: sets build stage IN (Newly built, Renovated, Previously owned) in one tap; _ suppresses the handover pickers and the Handover Delivery Stage selector while active. — PRD §6.3–6.5 pp28–32 — RQS-03 §3 pp66 — P1 — S3 — Unverified — Live at launch.

- [ ] **AUD-RQS03-0073** — Handover Delivery Stage: allowed values Site Preparation & Substructure: Site Clearing & Excavation; Foundation Footing; DPC (German Floor) Carcass: Blockwork / Lintel Level; Decking; Roofing / Parapet Semi- Finished: Lock-up; First-Fix Infrastructure Finishing: POP Ceiling; Tiling & Floor Finishes; Second-Fix Installation; Screeding & Painting Commissioning, External Works & Handover: External Works & Services; Snagging & Inspection; Handover. Control Grouped Multi-Select Checkboxes (OR). Rules Default: Any. Dependent: renders only when “Off-plan” or “Under construction” is active; hidden and cleared otherwise. Identifies the construction milestone a development has reached across five standard Nigerian phases; selecting a phase header selects all of its milestones. These milestones commonly determine when off-plan instalments fall due (the DPC stage is almost always a major payment trigger). Milestone definitions are given below this table. — PRD §6.3–6.5 pp28–32 — RQS-03 §3 pp66 — P1 — S3 — Unverified — Live at launch.

Month granularity replaces the current day-level completion window. — PRD §6.3–6.5 pp28–32 — RQS-03 §3 pp66 — P1 — S3 — Unverified — Live at launch.

- [ ] **AUD-RQS03-0075** — Bedrooms Boundary: allowed values Min: Any, 1+, 2+, 3+, 4+, 5+, 6+ Optional Max: Any, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6+. Control Segmented Min + Dropdown Max. Rules Default: Any. Inert when Minimum is “Any”. — PRD §6.3–6.5 pp28–32 — RQS-03 §3 pp66 — P1 — S3 — Unverified — Live at launch.

Toilets frequently exceed full bathrooms. Drawer only; kept off the bar popover. — PRD §6.3–6.5 pp28–32 — RQS-03 §3 pp66 — P1 — S3 — Unverified — Live at launch.

## 19. Acceptance and Verification Plan

Use each primary entry as one acceptance record with source page, test data, role/profile, expected outcome, provider/backend trace, evidence and sign-off. A test that only asserts a matching component name is insufficient.

| Module | Functional/integration verification | Permission/edge/regression verification |
|---|---|---|
|RQS-01 projects/purchase|Actual hierarchy/details, progress16 milestones, enquiry/terms, bundle allocation, independent/shared releases and receipts|Two-buyer race; revoked authority; unit removal/dispute; revised dates; mobile track; failure/refund retry|
|RQS-02 onboarding|Every field ID/option/condition/default, inheritance/override, import row errors, publishing and cover|Draft vs publish; commercial null rooms; negative/POA/date/coordinate cases; inherited changes; large unit-table behaviour|
|RQS-03 discovery|Full-catalogue strict-AND search, tokens/facets/filter dependencies, result bounds/counts/map clusters, URL restore|Off-by-default map search; hover sync; no GBP/sqft; no false zero matches; empty/error/loading; responsive keyboard operation|
|RQS-04 individual|Every step and conditional field, migration, validation, status/title/media and approved publish rules|Permissions, room applicability, title privacy, location boundary, retained stale stock, POA/reserve distinctions|
|RQS-05 Compare|Eligibility, persistent tray/sets, mobile cards, all attribute rows, FX/freshness, intelligent suggestions/insights|POA/null, mixed categories, changed/withdrawn stock, login merge, limit and removal states; genuine full-store retrieval|
|RQS-06 portals/services|All profile/seat task flows, viewing/proxy/Zoom, documents, escrow/register/trust, feeds/promotions, Console, finance and ecosystem|Cross-profile/IDOR/role escalation; contact blocking; consent withdrawal; event replay; prep/approve denial; every external provider failure|
|RQS-07 profiles|Every family and F1–F43 checklist cross-reference, privacy, public actions/content/rating eligibility|Guest/Registered/Verified gates; no empty/zero ratings; hidden email/phone/reserve; follow/report actions and responsive layout|
|RQS-08 fees|All11808-* acceptance rows and23 products with approved Console versions, routes, invoices and ledger|Tax liability, USD/NGN, fee recovery, renewal/grace, waiver/refund, past-rate snapshot, idempotency and revenue recognition|
|NFR/launch|Realistic search/bulk data and slow networks, accessibility audit, backup restore, incident/deploy/rollback rehearsal|Three themes; keyboard/screenreader; XSS/upload/session/rate checks; secrets/log redaction; downtime/provider fallback|


Test matrix: Guest, Registered, Verified Buyer, Owner, Developer, Agency agent/seat, each enabled Partner category, and each Console department/approver; desktop/tablet/mobile; supported browsers; NGN/USD; normal/outage/retry states. Use named specified providers only. Run sandbox money flows with no production charges until commercial/provider approval. Independent QA and Samuel UAT should sign module/source coverage and financial reconciliation; pass the full existing suite again after changes and inspect tests encoding superseded legacy behaviour. Production smoke tests must verify API origin/TLS, access flags, credentials, deliverability, logging and monitoring without leaking or broadcasting real data.

## 20. Audit Limitations and Confidence

This report is extensive but **does not certify a complete production or full-backend audit**. All354 required PDF pages were text-examined and all labelled diagrams inspected; every page was rendered. Multi-column table extraction was repaired with cell extraction and selected visual inspection. Not every extracted table cell was independently rechecked at full rendered-page resolution, and not every source/test line was read. Therefore the field inventory must receive a source-cell confirmation during implementation, particularly continuation rows and overlapping publication rules. No knowingly unread required PDF page is hidden.

Requirement granularity: counts are primary, source-bound acceptance/delivery entries, including individual field/search/fee/document tasks and shared platform/operational constraints. A global invariant and its context-specific UI/application task are different verification units; repeated explanatory text does not create a second primary ID. Broad module behaviours are sometimes grouped where one outcome needs a coherent state machine. This inventory must not be represented as a mathematically unique count of every possible acceptance assertion. Stable IDs are assigned in this report; maintain them in subsequent tracking rather than regenerate numbering after edits.

Generic group evidence establishes owning implementation and its boundaries, not positive proof of every clause. Status Unverified is intentionally used where a precise per-rule source/runtime proof was not established. Unknown backend implementation is not marked Missing merely because a frontend control is absent. The sibling backend inspection is selective; architecture/deployment/DB/provider review remains required. No browser runtime, real provider sessions, production accounts, legal validity, signed contract variations or actual staffing were verified.
